nodes.label: ADR-0001 doc: Shared curriculum per Subject
nodes.author: Bruno Martins
nodes.norm_label: adr-0001 doc: shared curriculum per subject

nodes.label: Decision: Shared curriculum per Subject, not per-user generation
nodes.author: Bruno Martins
nodes.rationale: Every user of a Subject gets the same Lessons/Rubrics, generated once and reviewed; per-user generation was rejected because the Evaluator needs one reviewable Rubric per Project, so per-user rubrics would make grading consistency and QA unbounded.
nodes.norm_label: decision: shared curriculum per subject, not per-user generation

nodes.label: ADR-0002 doc: GitHub Actions as Evaluator sandbox
nodes.author: Bruno Martins
nodes.norm_label: adr-0002 doc: github actions as evaluator sandbox

nodes.label: Decision: GitHub Actions as the Evaluator's execution sandbox
nodes.author: Bruno Martins
nodes.rationale: Uses GitHub Actions rather than self-hosting a Docker/gVisor/Firecracker sandbox, avoiding building and hardening untrusted-code execution while staying free at current scale; requires verifying the Submission's workflow file matches the Template Repo's before running, or a user could fake a pass.
nodes.norm_label: decision: github actions as the evaluator's execution sandbox

nodes.label: ADR-0003 doc: PWA over native mobile for v1
nodes.author: Bruno Martins
nodes.norm_label: adr-0003 doc: pwa over native mobile for v1

nodes.label: Decision: PWA over native mobile for v1
nodes.author: Bruno Martins
nodes.rationale: Shipped as PWA since Web Push satisfies closed-app notifications on Android and iOS 16.4+ without app-store distribution; iOS requires manual home-screen install since Apple provides no programmatic install prompt, so onboarding must detect standalone mode and guide iOS users.
nodes.norm_label: decision: pwa over native mobile for v1

nodes.label: ADR-0004 doc: Polyglot stack, split-ecosystem monorepo
nodes.author: Bruno Martins
nodes.norm_label: adr-0004 doc: polyglot stack, split-ecosystem monorepo

nodes.label: Decision: Rails backend + React frontend, split-ecosystem pnpm monorepo
nodes.author: Bruno Martins
nodes.rationale: Chose Rails (apps/api, Bundler) + React/Vite (apps/web, pnpm) over a single TypeScript stack because the user deliberately wants Rails experience, not just the fastest path to shipping; consequence is two dependency ecosystems/toolchains and no shared types without an explicit contract.
nodes.norm_label: decision: rails backend + react frontend, split-ecosystem pnpm monorepo

nodes.label: ADR-0005 doc: Solid Queue as Active Job backend
nodes.author: Bruno Martins
nodes.norm_label: adr-0005 doc: solid queue as active job backend

nodes.label: Decision: Solid Queue over Sidekiq for background jobs
nodes.author: Bruno Martins
nodes.rationale: Solid Queue is Postgres-backed, reuses the existing DB, needs no separate Redis, and is the Rails 8 Active Job default; consistent with the free/minimal-infra approach used elsewhere (GitHub Actions over self-hosted sandboxing, PWA over native). Consequence: no built-in job dashboard (needs Mission Control Jobs), explicit retry_on needed, and enqueue_after_transaction_commit needed for jobs enqueued inside a DB transaction.
nodes.norm_label: decision: solid queue over sidekiq for background jobs

nodes.label: Node ID format spec ({stem}_{entity})
nodes.rationale: IDs must use the full repo-relative path (every directory level) joined with the entity name so the LLM-generated ID matches the AST extractor's ID exactly; using only the filename or immediate parent creates orphan ghost-duplicate nodes, and IDs must never carry chunk-number suffixes so they stay deterministic.

nodes.label: Confidence-score rubric (discrete values)
nodes.rationale: Requires picking one of five fixed values (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) for INFERRED edges instead of a free continuous range, because production data showed models collapse a continuous 0-1 range into a bimodal split (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+); discrete rubrics are followed more faithfully.

nodes.label: Constrained query vocabulary expansion
nodes.rationale: graphify query matches via case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming/synonyms/cross-language match, so a wording mismatch between the user's question and the graph's node-label vocabulary collapses the answer to zero hits; fixed by expanding the query against the graph's own extracted vocabulary before traversal, picking only tokens that already exist in that vocab (never inventing tokens).

nodes.label: reflect / LESSONS.md work-memory loop
nodes.rationale: save-result records each query/path/explain answer with an outcome (useful/dead_end/corrected); graphify reflect --if-stale regenerates LESSONS.md (preferred sources, dead ends, corrections) cheaply and deterministically so future sessions don't re-derive the same dead ends.

nodes.label: Semantic extraction cache (per-file, prompt-stamped)
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are attributed to the extraction-spec.md prompt file that produced them; when the prompt changes on a graphify upgrade, old-prompt entries are re-extracted instead of replayed, while unchanged-prompt entries keep being served from cache, avoiding redundant LLM calls on unchanged files.

nodes.label: Manifest stamping (only-on-output rule)
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files (docs/papers/images) that actually produced output this run are stamped in the manifest; a changed file whose chunk failed or was omitted stays unstamped so the next --update re-queues it, and dispatched-but-unstamped files have their stale semantic_hash cleared so they aren't mistaken for unchanged - otherwise their content would be permanently lost.

nodes.label: build_merge (incremental graph merge)
nodes.rationale: Reads graph.json directly (no NetworkX round-trip) so directed edge relations survive merges; prune_sources is applied only to genuinely deleted files (never changed files) because replace-on-re-extract already drops every source_file present in the new chunk from the base before merging in the fresh version.

nodes.label: graph.json shrink guard
nodes.rationale: to_json() refuses to write graph.json if the new graph has fewer nodes than the existing one, and downstream report/analysis files are only written when the write actually happened - so a broken or partial extraction can never silently overwrite a good graph.

nodes.label: Issue tracker
nodes.rationale: Issues live in this repo's GitHub Issues, managed via the gh CLI.

nodes.label: Triage labels
nodes.rationale: Five canonical triage labels (needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix) give a default categorization scheme.

nodes.label: Domain docs
nodes.rationale: Single-context layout keeps domain knowledge co-located: CONTEXT.md plus docs/adr/ at the repo root.

nodes.label: Dev environment (AGENTS.md)
nodes.rationale: All development, including Claude Code itself, runs inside the project's dev container, never on the host, for environment consistency.

nodes.label: Feature workflow (Matt Pocock skills main flow)
nodes.rationale: Steps 1-3 (grill-with-docs, to-spec, to-tickets) are kept in one unbroken context window so grilled decisions carry through spec and tickets without being lost to compaction; implement starts fresh per ticket.
nodes.norm_label: feature workflow (matt pocock skills main flow)

nodes.label: Commit style
nodes.rationale: Commitizen/Conventional Commits format (type(scope): description, imperative, lowercase, no trailing period) keeps commit history consistent and parseable; add a body when the why isn't obvious.

nodes.label: graphify (AGENTS.md)
nodes.rationale: graphify query/path/explain return a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output, so it is preferred first for codebase questions.
